newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany launches new growth stock market.
newsitem.headline: Germany launches new growth stock market.

text.p: The German stock exchange on Tuesday unveiled details of its forthcoming new market for growth stocks, its latest bid to promote equity trading activity and encourage more small firms to go public.
Designed to appeal to risk-friendly investors at home and abroad, the market will be launched on the Frankfurt trading floor in early March next year.

Interested firms, which the bourse says will be both small and mid-sized, will have to satisfy strict requirements to take part in the scheme, including even tougher rules on transparency than those applying to regular listings.
Such firms would find it difficult to generate enough investor interest in the existing over-the-counter market to which their shares would most likely be confined.

"The fact that we have defined the tough criteria five months before the start will give the candidates more than enough time to get themselves fit," said stock exchange board member Reto Francioni in a statement.
The minimum issue volume is 10 million marks, of which at least half should derive from a capital increase. At least 15 percent of the shares, preferably 25 percent, must be distributed broadly.

In addition, companies must commit themselves to publishing quarterly earnings reports in German and English following either International Accounting Standards (IAS) or U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
The bourse said the launch was a concerted initiative by businesses, politicians, banks and investors to develop a lasting international investor pool for German growth stocks.
Similar initiatioves were under way in France and Brussels and there were long term plans to harmonise the European growth stock markets and develop electronic links between them.

"The capital raised will lay the basis to realise existing growth potential and ... allow staff and management to take part in company success -- an important form of motivation especially for dynamic companies," the exchange said.
Companies will be supported by a so-called "guardian" -- a similar role to a market maker -- to advise it on procedures and provide sell and buy price quotes for investors once trading begins.
